tip.worthNote: The balances of your bank accounts, wallets and the accounts you track yourself, as the bank last reported them. Credit cards are not included.
tip.missingNote: An account with no balance yet counts as 0 until a sync reads it.
tip.incomeNote: All money that came in. Transfers between your own accounts are not counted.
tip.expensesNote: All spending. Card bill payments and transfers between your own accounts are not counted, because the purchases are already counted.
tip.netNote: What you kept this month. A minus means you spent more than came in.
tip.cardNote: What you have bought with this card this month so far, compared with last month.
tip.wiseNote: What you have paid with your Wise card this month so far, compared with last month. It leaves your Wise balance right away, so nothing is charged later.
tip.jarsNote: Money you have put aside on purpose. It stays in your accounts but is not for spending.
tip.cushionNote: Your cushion. The jars never use it and it is not counted as spendable.
tip.otherNote: The smaller places your money goes.
tip.noteBudget: Left in budget is what remains of this budget for the month. It is not your total money left. What is unused at the end of the month can go into jars.
tip.noteBill: Left to pay is what remains of this month's bills. It is not your total money left. What is unused at the end of the month can go into jars.
tip.noteUsual: Left of usual is what remains of your usual spending here. It is not your total money left. What is unused at the end of the month can go into jars.
tip.jarNoRecount: Amounts a jar already pays are not counted again here.
tip.unplannedNote: Spending in categories that have no budget and no usual monthly amount yet, so nothing was planned for them. It is already out of your balance.
tip.startBarAct: Your balance today plus what you have already spent this month. Each bar after this takes off what you really spent.
tip.startBarPlan: Your balance today plus what you have already spent this month. Each bar after this takes off the budget (or usual month) of that item.
tip.startStepAct: Your balance today plus what you have already spent this month. Each step takes off what you really spent.
tip.startStepPlan: Your balance today plus what you have already spent this month. Each step takes off the full budget (or usual month) of that item.
tip.shortNote: Saved money and planned spending add up to more than your accounts.
tip.freeNote1: Money in your accounts that is not put aside or planned for anything, so it is free to spend or save.
tip.freeNote2: Jars take this money on their own while they have room, so it is often ₪0.
tip.availNote1: Money in your accounts right now that is not put aside in jars.
tip.availNote2: Bills and budgets still to come are not taken off yet.
tip.asideNote: Money you marked as not for spending. It stays in your accounts.
tip.spentTileNote: What you have already spent this month, by budget and category.
tip.plannedTileNote: The full budget (or usual month) of each item, and the bills of this month. An item already over its budget counts what you spent. What a jar already pays is not counted again.

al.gapUp: {n}: balance went up by {amt} with no matching transaction

al.cardDown: {n}: you owe {amt} more on this card with no matching purchase
al.cardUp: {n}: you owe {amt} less on this card with no matching payment
al.cardUpX: Usually the card bill was paid from an account that is not connected here, and then nothing is wrong. It can also be a refund the card has not listed yet.
al.pendingX: Pending charges are not settled by the bank yet. They are already counted in the balance and listed in Activity as pending. This goes away by itself when they settle.
al.feLogon: The bank gave no answer to the login request, so the app could not log in. This is usually the bank’s bot protection blocking the app’s browser, or a short block after several tries. Wait an hour, then press Test connection once. Press “See where it stopped” to see what the app’s browser saw. Until then, use the CSV export (Settings → Import and export).
al.feNoData: The bank accepted the login but sent back no data. Usually the bank wants something first: a code, a new-device check, a new password, or a notice. Or it blocks automatic access. Log in on the bank's website yourself to see what it asks for. If it asks nothing, press “See where it stopped” on the connection to see what the app’s browser saw. Until then, use the CSV export (Settings → Import and export).
al.feOtp: The bank asked for a one-time code by SMS, so automatic sync is paused. Press Verify this device once. Log in in the live window, enter the code, and tick “remember this device”. Banks usually only ask on a device they do not know. (Or use a CSV export: Settings → Import and export.)
al.uncatX: Give them a category, or make a rule so it happens by itself.
al.docsX: {amt}. Income with no invoice or receipt attached. Attach one if you need it for your books (you can turn this alert off in Alert settings).

diag.title: What this is based on:
diag.main: income about {inc} a month and expenses about {exp} a month, from {span} ({months}). {cur} so far is not included. Positive amounts count as income and negative ones as expenses, whatever their category. Income that arrives in two or more months counts as recurring. It is estimated from the months it really arrived, including this month so far. Income that arrived in only one month (a one-off, like a refund or a single transfer) is left out, because it would not repeat.
diag.cards: 1 credit card bill payment from the bank is left out, because the purchases are already counted on the card. | {n} credit card bill payments from the bank are left out, because the purchases are already counted on the card.
diag.only: Only 1 complete month of history exists, so that is what is used. | Only {n} complete months of history exist, so that is what is used.
diag.zero: No income was found in {months}. If you expected income, your history may be incomplete. Try Import history in Settings → Connections.

forecast.methodLine: Method: {how} of {span} with data, per source and category.

how.smart: smart estimate (unusually big or small months are pulled toward the typical month, and a trend counts only a little, for a few months ahead)

j.short: Planned {planned} a month, but the free money expected only allows about {avg} a month on average.

forecast.jarFoot: Jars can only take money that is really free. This starts with {free} free today and adds the surplus the forecast above expects each month (about {net} a month, income minus expenses, from {span}), shared by priority. Bill jars are assumed to stay full. If your income or spending changes, so do these numbers. The dashed line is the goal.

note.title: How this is calculated:
note.a: no AI. For each income source and expense category the app takes {span}.
note.b: projects the same monthly value forward.
note.c: extends the straight line through those months, limited to ±50% of the average. Each month, income minus expenses is added to today's bank + Wise balance (in ₪). The pension is not part of the forecast. One-off items, like a trip, are only included if they happened in the months used.
